primary_diagnosis_treated: Metabolic-syndrome-driven primary hypertension with dyslipidaemia and prediabetes

medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends ACE‑I as first‑line antihypertensive in patients <55 years without contraindications

medications.dose: 5 mg oral tablet once daily; increase to 10 mg after 2 weeks if BP >140/90 mmHg
medications.duration: Lifelong — review BP after 4 weeks, then every 6‑12 months
medications.purpose: Add‑on therapy for uncontrolled stage 2 hypertension
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 advises adding a CCB when BP remains uncontrolled on ACE‑I monotherapy

medications.duration: Lifelong — lipid profile at 3 months, then annually; increase to 40‑80 mg if LDL target not met
medications.purpose: Dyslipidaemia (LDL 140.5 mg/dL, HDL 24.6 mg/dL) and primary CVD risk reduction
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181/PH46 recommends high‑intensity statin for patients with QRISK ≥10% or ≥2 metabolic‑syndrome components

medications.dose: 500 mg oral tablet once daily with evening meal, titrate by 500 mg weekly to 500 mg twice daily (max 2 g/day) as tolerated
medications.purpose: Prediabetes with BMI ≥30 kg/m² to reduce progression to type 2 diabetes
medications.nice_justification: NICE PH38 advises metformin for high‑risk prediabetes when lifestyle alone insufficient

interactions_checked.interaction: Both metabolised by CYP3A4; amlodipine can increase atorvastatin AUC modestly
interactions_checked.action: Use atorvastatin 20 mg (low dose) and monitor for myopathy; check CK if muscle symptoms develop
Proceed; monitor renal function and eGFR after initiation

interactions_checked.interaction: No significant interaction; additive BP lowering possible
interactions_checked.action: Monitor BP and symptoms of hypotension after dose change

contraindications.reason: Can worsen glucose tolerance and lipid profile in metabolic syndrome
contraindications.alternative: Indapamide 1.5 mg MR if additional BP control needed

contraindications.reason: May mask hypoglycaemia and worsen metabolic parameters
No added benefit and increased renal risk (NICE NG136)
contraindications.alternative: Do not add an ARB while lisinopril is continued

contraindications.reason: Increase risk of renal impairment and fluid retention (NICE NG136, NG106)
contraindications.alternative: Use paracetamol for analgesia; avoid regular NSAIDs

contraindications.reason: Risk of fluid retention, contraindicated in patients with possible cardiac overload
contraindications.alternative: Metformin is preferred for glucose control

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided – assumed ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m²; obtain eGFR before starting metformin and before any dose escalation of lisinopril
Serum potassium not available – obtain baseline K+ before ACE‑I dose change and monitor after initiation of any RAAS‑modifying drug
Liver function tests not provided – obtain baseline ALT/AST before starting atorvastatin and repeat at 3 months
QRISK score not calculated – based on age, hypertension, obesity, low HDL, and prediabetes, risk is likely ≥10%; formal QRISK calculation required
Smoking and alcohol use not documented – assess and counsel as part of lifestyle intervention
Albumin‑to‑creatinine ratio not available – obtain to assess renal involvement of hypertension
Allergy history not documented – verify no sulfonamide or statin allergy before prescribing
treatment_summary: Add amlodipine to existing lisinopril for better BP control, start atorvastatin for dyslipidaemia, and initiate metformin for high‑risk prediabetes. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, liver enzymes, CK, and BP according to NICE NG136 and CG181. Provide lifestyle advice and arrange necessary baseline investigations.
